why: Explain how the host is connected and where traffic is expected to go.

why: Spot impending certificate expiry or certificate/identity validation failures.
when_to_use: Before renewals, during service onboarding or after certificate deployment.
decision_supported: Prioritise renewal or investigate trust, hostname and connectivity errors.
interpretation_limit: One verified endpoint is not complete TLS coverage; trust depends on local clock/store and revocation is not established.

purpose: Offline listener drift and vulnerability-export reconciliation
validation: Synthetic regression tests; Linux tested; native Windows/macOS validation pending
why: Expose listener-binding drift and changes between vulnerability exports without silently declaring closure.
when_to_use: After changes or between equivalent scheduled collections.
decision_supported: Investigate new observations, metadata changes and items no longer observed.
interpretation_limit: Normalised CSV required; absent findings are not confirmed fixed and scope/collector success need independent verification.

why: Turn effective SSH settings into review prompts while retaining authentication and access context.
when_to_use: When reviewing saved sshd -T output for a specific default or simulated connection context.
decision_supported: Select settings needing design/owner review before proposing changes.
interpretation_limit: Not a compliance baseline; does not prove the running daemon uses these settings or that MFA/reachability works.
validation: Synthetic parser regression tests; native Linux/macOS sshd collection validation pending

why: Record file identity and publisher-signature observations without running the files.
when_to_use: When checking software deliveries, suspected tampering or post-change binaries.
decision_supported: Select files needing provenance checks, sandbox analysis or vendor confirmation.
interpretation_limit: Valid is not safe; unsigned is not malicious; host trust and network/cache behaviour affect validation.
